questions.question: How should you position yourself to properly control a motorcycle?

options.text: Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Use your arms to hold up your body.
Keep your knees against the gas tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to help you balance during turns. Sit with your arms slightly bent and use them to steer, not to hold yourself up. This position lets you control all the motorcycle's controls easily.

questions.question: How fast does the human body remove alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour on average. This rate varies from person to person. The safest choice is to not ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: When you need to brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Do both actions at the same time.
Do one action, then the other.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: When you must both swerve and brake, do them separately. Brake first then swerve, or swerve first then brake. Never do both at the same time.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a turn?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed before entering a turn. Taking a turn too fast can cause you to drift out of your lane or off the road.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: Protects your face, but not your eyes.
Protects your eyes, but not your whole face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face, including your eyes, in a crash. A windshield is not a good substitute.

questions.question: Which lane position best prevents other vehicles from sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your space. When following a car, riding in the center also makes you more visible in the car's rearview mirror, so the driver is more likely to see you.

questions.question: When crossing angled railroad tracks, what is usually best?

options.text: Use the road shoulder to slow down before crossing.
Walk your motorcycle across the tracks.
Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Ride straight within your lane to cross angled railroad or trolley tracks. Changing your path angle may push you into another lane and cause a collision with oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a DOT-approved helmet allow you to do?

options.text: See as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
Become a hazard to the rider.

questions.correctAnswerText: See as far to the sides as needed for safe riding.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not limit your vision. It allows you to see as far as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: What type of footwear should a rider wear?

options.text: Shoes that are below the ankles.
Boots or shoes that cover the ankles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Boots or shoes that cover the ankles.
questions.explanation: Choose sturdy footwear that covers and supports your ankles. Soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: When being passed, should you move away from the passing vehicle?

options.text: Yes, because you will be farther away from the passing vehicle.
No, because it may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.
It does not matter because it has no effect on safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, because it may cause the passing driver to return to your lane too early.
questions.explanation: Do not move away from a passing vehicle. Moving to the far side of your lane may prompt the passing driver to move back into your lane too early.

questions.question: What can a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protect you from?
questions.correctAnswerText: Dust.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your face in a crash. It also protects against pebbles thrown up by other vehicles, wind, dust, dirt, rain, and insects.

questions.question: When riding at night, what should you do?

options.text: Move closer to the vehicle in front of you so you can use its lights to see farther ahead.
Keep riding at your normal speed to lower the risk of being hit from behind.
Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and stay farther behind other vehicles. It is harder to see at night, so you need more time and space to react to hazards.

questions.question: Wearing what gives you the best chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash?
questions.correctAnswerText: Face or eye protection.
questions.explanation: A helmet is your best defense against injury while riding. A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield helps protect your face from injury in a crash.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, what should riders do?

options.text: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
Ignore the stop line and move forward to get a better look.
Stop at the stop line then proceed through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop at the stop line, then move forward slowly to see cross traffic better.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection with a stop line or stop sign, stop where indicated. Then move forward slowly and stop again just before the crossroad. Lean forward and look around buildings, parked cars, or bushes to check for traffic. Keep your front wheel out of the crossroad while looking.

questions.question: When your front tire goes flat, how does your steering feel?
questions.correctAnswerText: Heavy.
questions.explanation: If steering suddenly feels heavy, your front tire may be flat. Stop and check your tires as soon as possible.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Keep your hands ready on both the clutch and brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your hands ready on both the clutch and brakes.
questions.explanation: Ride carefully when approaching an intersection. Keep your hands ready on both the clutch and brakes so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does a solid white line on the side of the road mean?

options.text: The right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right edge of a traffic lane.
questions.explanation: A solid white line on the side of the road marks the right edge of a traffic lane.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
Travel on the shoulder to stay out of traffic.
Use only the rear brake because the front brake does not work on slippery surfaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves because they can cause a skid.
questions.explanation: On a slippery surface, sudden changes in speed or direction can cause a skid. Be smooth when you speed up, shift gears, turn, or brake.

questions.question: What formation should you use when riding in a group?
questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on the situation.
questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation. Switch to single-file when taking a curve, turning, entering a highway, or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?
questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of a motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should try to avoid obstacles on the road. If avoiding an obstacle is not possible, what should they do?

options.text: Speed up before hitting the object.
Stay seated so the seat cushions some of the impact.
Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the obstacle at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down first. Try to approach it at a 90-degree angle whenever possible.

questions.question: Hearing protection is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Recommended for all rides.
questions.explanation: Wind and engine noise can damage your hearing over time, even with a helmet. Wear hearing protection on every ride to protect your ears.

questions.question: A good lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen and avoid hazards. It should prevent other drivers from trying to share your lane, not invite them into it. It should also give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: In areas where dangers could be present, a motorcyclist should:

options.text: Hold the clutch and both brake levers ready to reduce reaction time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the clutch and both brake levers ready to reduce reaction time.
questions.explanation: In dangerous areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Keep your clutch and both brake levers ready so you can react quickly in an emergency.

questions.question: A plastic face shield is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Not required, but recommended.
questions.explanation: Wear a plastic face shield on your helmet to protect your face and eyes while riding. Full face shields offer the best protection.

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All riders and passengers must wear a helmet when riding a motorcycle, motor-driven cycle, or motorized bicycle.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should not rely only on mirrors because:

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and limit your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Mirrors alone are not enough to stay aware of your surroundings. Motorcycles have blind spots just like any other vehicle.

questions.question: You should use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch when:

options.text: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
You start to lose control in a curve.

questions.correctAnswerText: The throttle is stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch right away. This removes power from the rear wheel so you can safely stop.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should focus on your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in the blind spots of large trucks. Remember: if you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.

questions.question: Most motorcycle and car accidents happen:
questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections.
questions.explanation: Most crashes between motorcycles and cars happen at intersections. Usually, the car driver fails to give the right-of-way to the motorcyclist.
